title: `parse` pays its whole setup on every call, and its ledger row is two orders of magnitude above `format`'s over the same table.
text: The cost is fixed per call rather than per byte — parsing an empty document costs what parsing a two-record one costs — and the only per-call work of that size is the DFA `csv_core::ReaderBuilder::build` constructs above the read loop. The figures are the ledger's, in `docs/perf/members.ndjson` under `rule:testing/member-perf-ledger`, measured by `benches/members/core/Csv/parse.nvs` and `format.nvs`. A program that parses one upload pays it once and cannot see it; one that parses a document per row of a report pays it per row, and `rows` — which builds one reader for a whole file — is the member that already avoids it. The fix is a reader cached per dialect and reset per call, which is a decision about what a native member may hold between calls rather than an edit to this one.
